questions.q: At what point will Yahweh forgive Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh will forgive Jerusalem if the prophet can find one person who is acting justly.

questions.q: When the people swear an oath in Yahweh’s name, what are they doing?
questions.a: They are swearing falsely; they are lying.

questions.q: Even though Yahweh has completely defeated the people, what do they still do?
questions.a: They still refuse to receive discipline.

questions.q: Why does the prophet say that these are only poor, foolish people?
questions.a: They do not know Yahweh’s ways.

questions.q: Do the important people know Yahweh’s ways?
questions.a: Yes, but they have rebelled against him anyway.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah say about the people’s transgressions and acts of faithlessness?
questions.a: Jeremiah said their transgressions were increasing and their acts of faithlessness were numerous.

questions.q: What have the sons of Judah done, according to Yahweh?
questions.a: They have abandoned Yahweh and sworn by false gods.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say each man desired?
questions.a: Each man desired his neighbor’s wife, like a well-fed horse desiring a mate.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do because of the people’s sins?
questions.a: He says he will punish them and take revenge on that nation.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say to do to the vines, but not completely?
questions.a: He says to remove the vines but not destroy them completely, because they do not belong to Yahweh.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, how have Israel and Judah acted toward him?
questions.a: They have betrayed him; they have been very unfaithful to him.

questions.q: What did the people say about Yahweh?
questions.a: They said he would not punish them or send war or famine against them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the prophets’ words?
questions.a: He says their words are like wind; they have no true message from God.

questions.q: What will Yahweh’s message become, and what will the people become?
questions.a: Yahweh’s message will become like fire, and the people will become like wood that the fire burns up.

questions.q: What is Yahweh about to do to the house of Israel?
questions.a: He is about to bring a nation against them from far away.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the invading nation’s soldiers?
questions.a: He says they are all warriors whose arrows will kill many people.

questions.q: What will the enemies do to the Israelites?
questions.a: The enemies will kill the Israelites’ children, take their animals, consume their food and food sources, and destroy their cities.

questions.q: What will Yahweh not do to his people, even in those days of punishment?
questions.a: He will not make a complete end of them.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh harm Israel and Judah?
questions.a: He will harm them because they abandoned Yahweh and worshiped foreign gods.

questions.q: Where is Jeremiah told to declare Yahweh’s message?
questions.a: He is told to declare it to the house of Jacob and announce it in Judah.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say his foolish people have but do not really use?
questions.a: He says they have eyes, but do not see, and ears but do not hear.

questions.q: What has Yahweh set as a lasting border that the sea cannot cross?
questions.a: He has set sand along the shore, and the sea’s waves cannot cross over it.

questions.q: What kind of heart does this people have, according to Jeremiah?
questions.a: They have a stubborn and rebellious heart, and they have turned aside and walked away.

questions.q: What does Yahweh want to do for those who fear him?
questions.a: He wants to give the rain at the right times and keep the harvest seasons in order.

questions.q: What has kept good things, like rain and harvest, from the people?
questions.a: Their iniquities and sins have kept the good things from them.

questions.q: What do the wicked people among Yahweh’s people do to others?
questions.a: They hide and set traps to capture people, like hunters who trap birds.

questions.q: Are the wicked among Yahweh’s people rich or poor?
questions.a: They are rich.

questions.q: How will Yahweh treat the wicked?
questions.a: He will punish them.

questions.q: What has happened in the land, according to Jeremiah?
questions.a: Desolation and horror has happened in the land.

questions.q: How do the people feel about what the prophets and priests do?
questions.a: They love it that way.

commentary.text: The Jews' profession of religion was hypocritical. (Jer. 5:1-9) The cruel proceedings of their enemies. (Jer. 5:10-18) Their apostacy and idolatry. (Jer. 5:19-31)

Jer. 5:1-9 None could be found who behaved as upright and godly men. But the Lord saw the true character of the people through all their disguises. The poor were ignorant, and therefore they were wicked. What can be expected but works of darkness, from people that know nothing of God and religion? There are God's poor, who, notwithstanding poverty, know the way of the Lord, walk in it, and do their duty; but these were willingly ignorant, and their ignorance would not be their excuse. The rich were insolent and haughty, and the abuse of God's favours made their sin worse.

Jer. 5:10-18 Multitudes are ruined by believing that God will not be so strict as his word says he will; by this artifice Satan undid mankind. Sinners are not willing to own any thing to be God's word, that tends to part them from, or to disquiet them in, their sins. Mocking and misusing the Lord's messengers, filled the measure of their iniquity. God can bring trouble upon us from places and causes very remote. He has mercy in store for his people, therefore will set bounds to this desolating judgment. Let us not overlook the "nevertheless," Jer. 5:18. This is the Lord's covenant with Israel. He thereby proclaims his holiness, and his utter displeasure against sin while sparing the sinner, Ps. 89:30-35.

Jer. 5:19-31 Unhumbled hearts are ready to charge God with being unjust in their afflictions. But they may read their sin in their punishment. If men will inquire wherefore the Lord doeth hard things unto them, let them think of their sins. The restless waves obeyed the Divine decree, that they should not pass the sandy shores, which were as much a restraint as lofty mountains; but they burst all restraints of God's law, and were wholly gone into wickedness. Neither did they consider their interest. While the Lord, year after year, reserves to us the appointed weeks of harvest, men live on his bounty; yet they transgress against him. Sin deprives us of God's blessings; it makes the heaven as brass, and the earth as iron. Certainly the things of this world are not the best things; and we are not to think, that, because evil men prosper, God allows their practices. Though sentence against evil works is not executed speedily, it will be executed. Shall I not visit for these things? This speaks the certainty and the necessity of God's judgments. Let those who walk in bad ways consider that an end will come, and there will be bitterness in the latter end.
